finding.title: Harness eval labeller still uses the previous session-mention grammar; the server now routes bare '<label>:' leads as mentions
finding.body: The server's new session-mention grammar routes a message that starts with a bare "<label>:" lead as a session mention, by rule. The harness copy of that grammar, which the eval labeller uses, is still the previous version. Until it moves, judgment-eval scores label-form roots that the server now routes as mentions by rule, which corrupts the chat routing eval. The same drift happened once before. Fix (one change): bump the harness grammar to the new version, add the server's parity vectors to the self-test, and sweep every mention of the old version in the contract and the eval tool.

Run judgment-eval for the chat routing use case on the confirmed labels. Record per-label thresholds or n/a, then apply them. Shadow for at least 3 days, or at least 20 new owner conversations, whichever is later. Switch on for the enabled labels only. Annotate the dated routing agreement: new owner conversations now route server-side by an advisory topic judgment for the enabled labels, the rest stay as before; cite the judgments contract.

finding.title: judgment-eval cannot measure a question-set version before it deploys
finding.body: judgment-eval runs a use case against whatever question-set version the server has deployed, and a dev server has no model key. So a proposed question-set version cannot be measured before it merges and deploys. Measured today: a new version was merged and deployed with its acceptance number recorded as n/a; its post-deploy eval then missed the pre-registered bar. Every future new-version ticket hits the same gap. Fix direction: let judgment-eval score a candidate question set that is not the deployed one, without recording product calls; a version it cannot load is an error, never a silent fallback to the deployed set.

finding.title: A misrouted root the chat router claimed by topic cannot be freed; follow-ups keep reaching the wrong session
finding.body: In mode on, when the chat router delivers a new owner root by topic, it claims the root's thread for the inbox it chose. If that topic judgment was wrong, nothing can release or move the claim: the owner's follow-ups in that thread keep going to the misrouted session, which has to forward each one by hand. A recent change stops a forwarder from claiming an unclaimed thread, but cannot free a thread the router already claimed. Candidate fix: a reroute of a router-claimed root transfers the router's claim to the destination session; regression test: follow-ups then route to the destination.

finding.title: In mode on, the chat router never delivers a root it routes by topic
finding.body: With the routing judgment in mode on, the router records its topic decision for a new owner conversation but never delivers the root to the chosen inbox: every topic-routed conversation is lost, and no session sees it. Mode off is unaffected because it never routes by topic.
